title: Custom System Metrics with CloudWatch Agent & EC2
goal: Goal: Collect OS-level metrics (e.g., RAM memory utilization, disk space) that CloudWatch hypervisor metrics cannot see by default using the Unified CloudWatch Agent.

concepts.title: Hypervisor vs OS-Level Metrics
concepts.body: Hypervisor Metrics (Default): Collected from outside the VM without an agent (CPU utilization, Network I/O, Disk I/O). OS-Level Metrics (Custom): Collected inside the OS (RAM memory usage, swap space, mounted disk usage) requiring the CloudWatch Agent.

concepts.title: Unified CloudWatch Agent
concepts.body: Lightweight daemon installed inside EC2 instances or on-premises servers to collect system metrics and log files.

concepts.title: IAM Instance Profile Role
concepts.body: Grants the EC2 instance permissions to publish metric data to CloudWatch using the managed policy CloudWatchAgentServerPolicy.

concepts.title: CWAgent Custom Namespace
concepts.body: Metrics published by the CloudWatch Agent are stored under the custom metric namespace CWAgent in CloudWatch.

concepts.title: Hypervisor vs CloudWatch Agent Metrics Comparison Matrix
concepts.body: Metric CategoryHypervisor Metrics (Default / Free)CloudWatch Agent Metrics (Custom)Collection MechanismAgentless (Host Hypervisor level)Agent-based (Installed in OS)CPU UtilizationCollected nativelyCollected natively with per-core breakdownNetwork / Disk I/OCollected natively (Packets & bytes)Collected nativelyRAM / Memory UsageNOT AvailableCollected (mem_used_percent)Swap Space / Disk SpaceNOT AvailableCollected (disk_used_percent)On-Premises ServersNot supportedSupported (Hybrid Cloud metrics)

whyItMatters: This matters because distinguishing between CloudWatch hypervisor metrics (CPU, Network, Disk I/O) vs. OS-level custom metrics (Memory/RAM utilization, swap usage, disk space) requiring the CloudWatch Agent is a classic SAA-C03 exam scenario.
costWarning: CloudWatch custom metrics, detailed monitoring, alarms, dashboards, Logs ingestion and storage, Logs Insights queries, Synthetics and connected-service charges may apply.

instructions.text: Sign in to the AWS Management Console.

Sign in to the AWS Management Console using an IAM user or lab role with appropriate permissions.

consoleSteps.title: Create IAM Role for CloudWatch Agent

instructions.text: Open IAM Console -> Choose Roles -> Click Create role.
Select Trusted entity type AWS service -> Select Use case EC2.
Search for and attach managed policy CloudWatchAgentServerPolicy.
Set Role name to EC2-CloudWatchAgent-Role -> Click Create role.

consoleSteps.note: Grants EC2 permissions to push metric data to CloudWatch.

consoleSteps.title: Launch EC2 Instance and Attach IAM Role

instructions.text: Open Amazon EC2 Console -> Click Launch instance.
Set Name to saa-cwagent-demo and select Amazon Linux 2023 AMI.
Select Instance type t2.micro (or t3.micro).
Under Advanced details -> IAM instance profile, select EC2-CloudWatchAgent-Role.
Click Launch instance.

consoleSteps.note: Attaching the instance profile authorizes the CloudWatch Agent daemon.

consoleSteps.title: Install and Start CloudWatch Agent via EC2 User Data or SSM

instructions.text: Connect to instance via EC2 Instance Connect.
Download CloudWatch Agent package: sudo yum install -y amazon-cloudwatch-agent.
Create minimal agent configuration file /opt/aws/amazon-cloudwatch-agent/bin/config.json enabling mem_used_percent and disk_used_percent.
Start CloudWatch Agent service: sudo /opt/aws/amazon-cloudwatch-agent/bin/amazon-cloudwatch-agent-ctl -a fetch-config -m ec2 -c file:/opt/aws/amazon-cloudwatch-agent/bin/config.json -s.

consoleSteps.note: Initializes agent daemon to collect OS-level memory and disk metrics.

consoleSteps.title: Verify Custom Memory Metrics in CloudWatch Console

instructions.text: Open Amazon CloudWatch Console -> Click Metrics in left navigation -> Choose All metrics.
Locate custom namespace CWAgent.
Select metric mem_used_percent for instance saa-cwagent-demo.
Confirm RAM memory utilization graph renders in real time.

consoleSteps.note: Validates that OS memory metrics appear under the CWAgent namespace.

consoleSteps.title: Tear down lab resources

instructions.text: Terminate EC2 instance saa-cwagent-demo.
Delete IAM role EC2-CloudWatchAgent-Role.

consoleSteps.warning: Terminate EC2 instances to stop compute billing.

cliSteps.expectedResult: Expected: account ID and IAM user/role ARN.

cliSteps.note: Lists custom metrics collected by CloudWatch Agent.

cheatSheet.title: Hypervisor Metrics
cheatSheet.body: CPU utilization, Network I/O, Disk I/O. Collected automatically without an agent.

cheatSheet.title: CloudWatch Agent Metrics
cheatSheet.body: RAM memory usage, swap utilization, mounted disk space. Requires installing CloudWatch Agent.

cheatSheet.title: Managed IAM Policy
cheatSheet.body: `CloudWatchAgentServerPolicy` provides required permissions for the agent daemon.

troubleshooting.title: Memory Metrics Missing in CloudWatch
troubleshooting.body: Verify that the EC2 instance has an IAM instance profile attached with `CloudWatchAgentServerPolicy` and that the agent service is running.

examTraps.title: Memory Metric Default Trap
examTraps.body: CloudWatch hypervisors do NOT collect RAM memory or disk space metrics by default. If an exam question asks to monitor RAM utilization, choose Install CloudWatch Agent.

examTips.text: SAA-C03: Master Amazon CloudWatch concepts and observability patterns in Amazon CloudWatch.

memoryHook: Hypervisor = CPU / Net / Disk I/O | CloudWatch Agent = RAM / Swap / Disk Space

title: Real-time Metric Filters, Alarms & SNS Notifications
goal: Goal: Monitor application log streams for specific error patterns and trigger automated notifications.

concepts.title: CloudWatch Log Groups & Streams
concepts.body: Log Groups contain multiple Log Streams emitted by application components, EC2 instances, or Lambda functions.

concepts.title: Metric Filters
concepts.body: Scans log events in real time for specific text strings or JSON patterns (e.g. `ERROR`, `500`, `[status=500]`) and increments a custom numerical metric.

concepts.title: CloudWatch Alarms
concepts.body: Monitors metric thresholds over specified time windows. Evaluates three states: `OK`, `IN_ALARM`, and `INSUFFICIENT_DATA`.

concepts.title: Amazon SNS Email Notifications
concepts.body: Triggers automated email or SMS notifications when a CloudWatch Alarm transitions into the `IN_ALARM` state.

concepts.title: Log Monitoring & Notification Pipeline Matrix
concepts.body: Pipeline StageAWS Service / ResourceRole & Description1. Log CollectionCloudWatch Log GroupReceives raw log entries from application instances2. Pattern ExtractionCloudWatch Metric FilterParses log stream text and extracts custom numeric metrics3. Threshold EvaluationCloudWatch AlarmEvaluates metric values against static or anomaly thresholds4. Notification DispatchAmazon SNS TopicSends email, SMS, or webhook alert notifications to subscribers

whyItMatters: This matters because the pattern of Log Metric Filters -> Custom Metric -> CloudWatch Alarm -> SNS Topic is a core SAA-C03 workflow.
costWarning: CloudWatch custom metrics, detailed monitoring, alarms, dashboards, Logs ingestion and storage, Logs Insights queries, Synthetics and connected-service charges may apply.

consoleSteps.title: Create CloudWatch Log Group and Stream Log Events

instructions.text: Open Amazon CloudWatch Console -> Click Log groups in left navigation -> Click Create log group.
Set Log group name to /aws/apps/saa-application-logs.
Click Create.
Open log group details -> Choose Log streams tab -> Click Create log stream.
Set Log stream name to app-stream-1 -> Click Create.

consoleSteps.note: Creates the target log group and stream for receiving application log events.

consoleSteps.title: Define Log Metric Filter for Error Terms

instructions.text: Open /aws/apps/saa-application-logs -> Choose Metric filters tab -> Click Create metric filter.
Under Filter pattern, enter ERROR.
Click Next.
Set Filter name to ErrorCountFilter.
Set Metric namespace to MyAppMetrics and Metric name to ErrorCount.
Set Metric value to 1 -> Click Create metric filter.

consoleSteps.note: Scans log events in real time and increments ErrorCount whenever ERROR appears.

consoleSteps.title: Create CloudWatch Alarm and Amazon SNS Topic

instructions.text: Select ErrorCountFilter -> Click Create alarm.
Set Threshold type to Static -> Whenever ErrorCount is Greater/Equal to 1 for 1 datapoint within 1 minute.
Click Next.
Under Alarm state trigger, select In alarm.
Select Create new topic -> Set Topic name to saa-error-alerts-topic.
Enter your Email address for notifications -> Click Create topic.
Set Alarm name to HighAppErrorRateAlarm -> Click Create alarm.
Open your email inbox and click Confirm subscription on the SNS confirmation email.

consoleSteps.note: Connects metric threshold breach to SNS email delivery.

consoleSteps.title: Simulate Application Error and Test SNS Notification

instructions.text: Open log stream app-stream-1 -> Click Actions -> Choose Create log event.
Paste test log entry: 2026-07-22 14:00:00 [ERROR] 500 Internal Server Error processing order #9941.
Click Create.
Monitor CloudWatch Alarm state transition from OK to In alarm.
Verify receipt of SNS alert email in your inbox.

consoleSteps.note: Validates that log errors automatically fire alarms and send email alerts.

consoleSteps.title: Tear down lab resources

instructions.text: Delete CloudWatch Alarm HighAppErrorRateAlarm.
Delete SNS Topic saa-error-alerts-topic.
Delete Log Group /aws/apps/saa-application-logs.

title: Network Traffic Analysis with VPC Flow Logs
goal: Goal: Capture and inspect IP traffic flowing to and from network interfaces in your VPC to troubleshoot Security Group and NACL rules.

concepts.title: VPC Flow Logs Overview
concepts.body: Feature that captures IP traffic flowing to and from network interfaces (ENIs) in a VPC, subnet, or specific network interface.

concepts.title: ACCEPT vs REJECT Traffic Actions
concepts.body: ACCEPT: Traffic allowed by both Security Groups and Network ACLs. REJECT: Traffic dropped by either a Security Group ingress/egress rule or a Network ACL rule.

concepts.title: Storage Destination Targets
concepts.body: Amazon S3: Most cost-effective target for long-term archiving and Athena SQL queries. CloudWatch Logs: Ideal for real-time metric filtering and alarms. Kinesis Data Firehose: Ideal for streaming to third-party SIEM tools.

concepts.title: Flow Log Record Fields
concepts.body: Captures metadata including `version`, `account-id`, `interface-id`, `srcaddr`, `dstaddr`, `srcport`, `dstport`, `protocol`, `bytes`, `packets`, `action`, `log-status`.

concepts.title: VPC Flow Log Destination Comparison Matrix
concepts.body: Destination TargetPrimary Use CaseAnalysis ToolingCost ProfileAmazon S3 BucketLong-term audit archiving & complianceAmazon Athena SQL queriesLowest cost (Supports S3 Lifecycle to Glacier)CloudWatch LogsReal-time metric filtering & immediate alertingCloudWatch Logs InsightsModerate cost (Ingestion & indexing fees)Kinesis Data FirehoseStreaming to external SIEM / Security toolsDatadog, Splunk, ElasticSearchVariable based on stream volume

whyItMatters: This matters because network troubleshooting (Security Group / NACL drops) using VPC Flow Logs and selecting cost-effective storage targets (S3 with Lifecycle rules vs CloudWatch Logs) is a core SAA-C03 topic.
costWarning: CloudWatch custom metrics, detailed monitoring, alarms, dashboards, Logs ingestion and storage, Logs Insights queries, Synthetics and connected-service charges may apply.

cheatSheet.title: REJECT Action

title: Distributed Microservice Tracing with AWS X-Ray
goal: Goal: Identify latency bottlenecks and service dependencies across distributed serverless or containerized microservices using AWS X-Ray Service Maps and Trace Timelines.

concepts.title: AWS X-Ray Overview
concepts.body: Distributed tracing service that collects data about requests served by microservices, providing a visual map of service dependencies and performance bottlenecks.

concepts.title: X-Ray Traces, Segments & Subsegments
concepts.body: Trace: Tracks an end-to-end request across all microservices. Segment: Data sent by a single compute component (e.g. API Gateway, Lambda, ECS). Subsegment: Detailed breakdown of downstream calls inside a segment (e.g., DynamoDB query time, HTTP API call duration).

concepts.title: X-Ray Service Map
concepts.body: Visual node connection graph displaying service health, average latency, and call volumes across microservice architectures.

concepts.title: Trace Context Header (X-Amzn-Trace-Id)
concepts.body: HTTP header passed between microservices to propagate trace context across network boundaries.

concepts.title: X-Ray Tracing Components Matrix
concepts.body: X-Ray ComponentFunctionDeployment PointX-Ray SDKInstruments application code, intercepts HTTP/database callsApplication code / Lambda functionX-Ray DaemonListens for UDP trace segments and batches uploads to X-Ray serviceEC2 instance, ECS container, Elastic BeanstalkActive Tracing ToggleNative 1-click integration without code changesAWS Lambda, Amazon API Gateway, AWS App Runner

whyItMatters: This matters because AWS X-Ray for distributed call tracing, performance bottlenecks, and service map visualization is a primary SAA-C03 exam topic.
costWarning: CloudWatch custom metrics, detailed monitoring, alarms, dashboards, Logs ingestion and storage, Logs Insights queries, Synthetics and connected-service charges may apply.

title: API Activity Auditing with AWS CloudTrail & Log Validation
goal: Goal: Audit user and API actions across all regions, enable log integrity validation, and detect anomalous API patterns with CloudTrail Insights.

concepts.title: Management Events vs Data Events
concepts.body: Management Events: Control plane operations (e.g. `RunInstances`, `CreateBucket`, `CreateUser`). Enabled by default. Data Events: High-volume resource operations (e.g. `s3:GetObject`, `s3:PutObject`, `lambda:Invoke`). Disabled by default due to log volume.

concepts.title: Log File Integrity Validation
concepts.body: CloudTrail signs delivered log files using SHA-256 hashing and digital signatures. Allows auditing whether log files were modified or deleted after delivery.

concepts.title: CloudTrail Insights
concepts.body: Analyzes baseline management event patterns and automatically flags unusual spikes in API call volume (e.g. sudden spike in `IAM:CreateUser` calls).

concepts.title: Multi-Region Trails
concepts.body: A single trail configuration that captures API calls across ALL AWS Regions automatically and consolidates logs into one S3 bucket.

concepts.title: CloudTrail Event Types & Validation Matrix
concepts.body: CloudTrail Event TypeScope & DescriptionDefault StatusCost ImplicationsManagement EventsControl plane operations (`Create`, `Modify`, `Delete` infrastructure)Enabled on first trailFirst copy free; additional trails $2 per 100k eventsData EventsData plane operations (`S3 GetObject`, `Lambda Invoke`)Disabled by defaultBilled at $0.10 per 100k eventsInsights EventsAutomated anomaly detection on API call volume spikesDisabled by defaultBilled at $0.35 per 100k analyzed events

whyItMatters: This matters because CloudTrail Management Events vs. Data Events (e.g., S3 object-level calls or Lambda executions) and enabling Digest Validation for compliance auditing are heavily tested on SAA-C03.
costWarning: CloudTrail additional event copies, data events, Insights, CloudTrail Lake, S3 storage, CloudWatch Logs and KMS charges may apply.

cheatSheet.title: Management Events
cheatSheet.body: Captures control plane operations (e.g. creating EC2 instances, modifying IAM roles). Enabled by default.

cheatSheet.title: Data Events
cheatSheet.body: Captures high-volume resource operations (e.g. S3 object reads/writes, Lambda invocations). Disabled by default.

cheatSheet.title: Log File Validation
cheatSheet.body: Uses cryptographic SHA-256 hashing and RSA signatures to prove log files haven't been tampered with.

troubleshooting.title: S3 Object Level Calls Missing in CloudTrail
troubleshooting.body: CloudTrail management events do NOT log S3 object downloads/uploads. You must explicitly enable **CloudTrail Data Events** for S3.

examTraps.title: S3 Data Events vs Management Events Trap
examTraps.body: If an exam scenario asks to audit S3 GetObject or PutObject API calls, do NOT rely on default CloudTrail settings. Select Enable CloudTrail Data Events.

examTips.text: SAA-C03: Master AWS CloudTrail concepts and observability patterns in AWS CloudTrail.

memoryHook: CloudTrail = Who Did What API Call | Digest Validation = Log Anti-Tamper Check

title: Automated Compliance & Remediation with AWS Config & EventBridge
goal: Goal: Automatically detect non-compliant resource configurations and trigger automated remediation using AWS Config, EventBridge, and SSM Automation.

concepts.title: AWS Config Overview
concepts.body: Service that continually assesses, audits, and evaluates resource configurations across your AWS account against compliance rules.

concepts.title: Config Managed Rules
concepts.body: Pre-built compliance definitions (e.g. s3-bucket-public-read-prohibited, encrypted-volumes) that evaluate resource settings continuously.

concepts.title: Compliance Drift & Resource History
concepts.body: Tracks historical configuration changes over time, recording exact timestamps when resources drifted into or out of compliance.

concepts.title: Automated Remediation
concepts.body: Pairs AWS Config compliance events with Systems Manager (SSM) Automation documents or EventBridge rules to automatically remediate non-compliant resources (e.g., auto-enabling S3 Block Public Access).

concepts.title: AWS Config vs CloudTrail vs GuardDuty Decision Matrix
concepts.body: AWS Governance ServicePrimary FunctionFocus AreaAWS ConfigResource Configuration History & Compliance DriftState evaluation (e.g. Is bucket public? Is disk encrypted?)AWS CloudTrailAPI Call Auditing & Governance LogAction evaluation (e.g. Who deleted the DB? When was instance stopped?)Amazon GuardDutyIntelligent Threat Detection & Anomaly AnalysisThreat detection (e.g. Malicious IP communication, compromised credentials)

whyItMatters: This matters because distinguishing AWS Config (resource configuration history and compliance drift) vs CloudTrail (API governance) vs GuardDuty (threat detection) is heavily tested on SAA-C03. Note: AWS Config evaluates resource compliance and records configuration changes, but does not prevent changes by itself without automated remediation actions.
costWarning: AWS Config configuration items, rule evaluations, conformance packs, aggregators, remediation and connected-service charges may apply.

consoleSteps.title: Set up the lab user and permissions

instructions.text: Sign in to the AWS Management Console.
Sign in to the AWS Management Console using an IAM user or lab role with appropriate permissions.
Sign in to the AWS Management Console using an IAM user or lab role with appropriate permissions.
For least privilege, use the grouped permissions below.

consoleSteps.warning: Do not leave broad admin access or long-term access keys in real company accounts.

consoleSteps.title: Enable AWS Config Recording

instructions.text: Open AWS Config Console -> Click Get started.
Under Resource types to record, select Record all current and future resource types.
Set Storage location to Create a bucket.
Set IAM role to Use an existing AWS Config service-linked role.
Click Next.

consoleSteps.note: Starts recording resource configuration changes across your account.

consoleSteps.title: Add Managed Compliance Rule (s3-bucket-public-read-prohibited)

instructions.text: Under Rules, click Add rule -> Search for s3-bucket-public-read-prohibited.
Select managed rule -> Click Next -> Click Save.
Wait for AWS Config to evaluate S3 bucket compliance across your account.

consoleSteps.note: Evaluates whether S3 buckets permit public read access.

consoleSteps.title: Simulate Non-Compliant Resource and View Compliance Drift

instructions.text: Create a test S3 bucket saa-non-compliant-bucket-[account-id].
Disable Block Public Access on the test bucket.
Return to AWS Config -> Trigger rule evaluation.
Verify rule status transitions to Non-compliant.

consoleSteps.note: Confirms AWS Config detects configuration drift into non-compliant state.

consoleSteps.title: Configure EventBridge Rule for Automated Remediation Notification

instructions.text: Open Amazon EventBridge Console -> Click Rules -> Click Create rule.
Set Name to saa-config-noncompliant-rule.
Set Event pattern: Service Config, Event type Config Rules Compliance Change, Detail {"newEvaluationResult":{"complianceType":["NON_COMPLIANT"]}}.
Attach Target: Select SNS Topic saa-error-alerts-topic.
Click Create rule.

consoleSteps.note: Routes compliance state changes to automated notification or SSM remediation.

consoleSteps.title: Tear down lab resources

instructions.text: Delete test S3 bucket saa-non-compliant-bucket-[account-id].
Delete EventBridge rule saa-config-noncompliant-rule.
Turn off AWS Config recorder and delete managed rule.

cliSteps.expectedResult: Expected: account ID and IAM user/role ARN.

cheatSheet.body: Assesses and audits resource configuration state and historical compliance drift over time.

cheatSheet.title: Automated Remediation
cheatSheet.body: Uses SSM Automation documents triggered directly by Config rules or EventBridge compliance events.

cheatSheet.title: Config vs CloudTrail
cheatSheet.body: Config tracks **resource configuration state**; CloudTrail logs **API call actions**.

troubleshooting.title: Rule Evaluation Delayed
troubleshooting.body: AWS Config rule evaluations run periodically or upon configuration changes. Click **Re-evaluate** in the Config console to force immediate evaluation.

examTraps.title: AWS Config vs CloudTrail Traps
examTraps.body: If an exam question asks to track **resource configuration drift and history**, do NOT select CloudTrail. Select AWS Config.

title: Deny S3 bucket deletion with an SCP
goal: Goal: Use an AWS Organizations Service Control Policy as an org guardrail to block s3:DeleteBucket in a member account.

concepts.title: SCP
concepts.body: Sets maximum available permissions for accounts/OUs.

concepts.title: Does not grant
concepts.body: SCPs never grant access by themselves.

concepts.title: Affects root
concepts.body: SCP deny affects all principals in member account, including root.

concepts.title: Guardrail
concepts.body: Best for coarse organization controls.

concepts.title: Explicit deny
concepts.body: SCP deny overrides IAM allow.

concepts.title: Fine control
concepts.body: Use IAM and resource policies for detailed access.

whyItMatters: SCPs are organization guardrails. They prevent risky actions even if a member account identity has an IAM allow. Note: SCPs specify maximum allowed permissions for member account principals, but do not grant permissions by themselves.
costWarning: AWS Organizations itself does not generally add a separate service charge, but services enabled across member accounts continue to incur normal charges.

consoleSteps.title: Before you start

instructions.text: Sign in to the management account.
Confirm SCPs are enabled in AWS Organizations.
Pick the target OU containing the child account.

consoleSteps.title: Create the SCP

instructions.text: Open AWS Organizations Policies.
Choose Service control policies.
Create policy named DenyDeleteBucket.
Paste the JSON below.

consoleSteps.title: Attach SCP to the OU

instructions.text: Open AWS accounts / Organize accounts.
Select the target OU.
Open Policies tab.
Attach DenyDeleteBucket.

consoleSteps.title: Create a safe test bucket in child account

instructions.text: Sign in to the child/member account.
Create bucket test-bucket-to-remove-12345.
Keep it empty or use only non-sensitive test data.

consoleSteps.title: Attempt delete from child account
consoleSteps.note: Expected: AccessDenied due to SCP.

consoleSteps.title: Tear down

instructions.text: Detach the SCP from the OU.
Delete the SCP if no longer needed.
Delete the test bucket after the SCP is removed.

commands.text:
aws organizations list-roots --profile orgroot

aws organizations list-organizational-units-for-parent \
  --parent-id r-ROOTID \
  --profile orgroot

aws organizations create-policy \
  --content file://deny-delete-bucket.json \
  --name DenyDeleteBucket \
  --type SERVICE_CONTROL_POLICY \
  --profile orgroot

aws organizations attach-policy \
  --policy-id p-POLICYID \
  --target-id ou-OU_ID \
  --profile orgroot

cliSteps.title: Create and delete test bucket from child

commands.text:
aws s3api create-bucket \
  --bucket test-bucket-to-remove-12345 \
  --create-bucket-configuration LocationConstraint=eu-west-2 \
  --profile child

aws s3api delete-bucket \
  --bucket test-bucket-to-remove-12345 \
  --profile child

cliSteps.note: Expected: delete fails due to SCP.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Expected: delete fails due to SCP.

cliSteps.title: Tear down

commands.text:
aws organizations detach-policy --policy-id p-POLICYID --target-id ou-OU_ID --profile orgroot
aws organizations delete-policy --policy-id p-POLICYID --profile orgroot
aws s3api delete-bucket --bucket test-bucket-to-remove-12345 --profile child
rm -f deny-delete-bucket.json

cliSteps.warning: Destructive Command Warning: This command permanently detaches permissions or deletes IAM identity resources.

cheatSheet.body: Account/OU guardrail.

cheatSheet.title: Does not grant

cheatSheet.body: Member root is also limited.

cheatSheet.title: Deny wins
cheatSheet.body: Overrides IAM allow.

cheatSheet.body: Use for org-wide restrictions.

troubleshooting.body: Wrong OU/account or SCP not attached.

troubleshooting.title: Still denied after detach
troubleshooting.body: Wait for propagation or check IAM/bucket policies.

troubleshooting.body: Use orgroot for Organizations and child for S3 test.

troubleshooting.body: Copy the p-... ID from create-policy.

examTraps.title: Trap 2
examTraps.body: SCPs affect root in member accounts.

examTraps.title: Trap 3
